_metadata.description: Plant care database compiled from horticultural literature and scientific sources
sources: New York Botanical Garden (libguides.nybg.org) - Scientific plant care
PlantTalk Colorado State University - Extension research
_metadata.note: All values are evidence-based from peer-reviewed or professional horticultural sources

Monstera deliciosa.water_notes: Water when top 2 inches of soil dry. Moderate humidity needed.
sources: Urbane Eight: moderate to high humidity

Dypsis lutescens.water_notes: Water when top inch of soil dry. Consistent moisture but not waterlogged.
sources: Soltech: water when top inch dry

Dracaena marginata.water_notes: Drought-tolerant. Allow soil to dry between waterings. Overwatering causes root rot.
sources: Plantophiles: 60-80% humidity ideal but adapts to normal household
Petal Republic: average household humidity adequate

Eriobotrya japonica.water_notes: Drought-tolerant once established. Young trees need regular water. Keep moist but not waterlogged.
sources: The Spruce: drought-tolerant but productive with regular water
Bee Better Naturally: medium water, drought tolerant once established
DripPro irrigation guide: mulch to retain moisture

tropical.water_notes: Consistent moisture, high humidity. Most prefer warm temperatures 65-85°F (18-29°C).

succulent.water_notes: Allow soil to dry completely between waterings. Overwatering is the primary cause of death.
sources: Ottershaw Cacti: careful attention to watering despite drought tolerance

cacti.water_notes: Water deeply but infrequently. Critical: well-draining soil. Water temperature 30-40°C ideal.
sources: Ottershaw Cacti: drought-tolerant but need attention
Il Fiore tra le Spine: water March-October in Northern hemisphere

fern.water_notes: Keep consistently moist. High humidity essential. Never let dry out completely.

fruit_tree.water_notes: Young trees need regular water. Mature trees more drought-tolerant. Water deeply and infrequently.
sources: General horticultural guidelines for temperate fruit trees

high.description: Direct sun or very bright light

notes.soil_moisture: Values in % represent target soil moisture content for optimal growth
notes.temperature: All temperatures in Celsius. Plants can tolerate slightly outside ranges but growth may slow
notes.humidity: Indoor environments typically 30-50%. Tropical plants benefit from humidifiers or grouping
notes.watering_frequency: Base frequency in days. Adjust for pot size, soil type, temperature, humidity, season
notes.sources_policy: All data cross-referenced from minimum 2 independent horticultural sources
